validation_checks: The Gate A card, project state, and selected design use the same cost posture, and a traceability check finds no weakened approved requirement.
The record contains the owner's exact cap and alert plan, or records `HARD_CAP_NOT_STATED` or why cost alerts do not apply.
The design records material billing dimensions and an attributable estimate or current-source calculation.
Each proposed expansion records a bounded threshold, evidence source, and owner decision path.
IaC and runbook checks cover approved tags, idle policy, and teardown or retained-resource behavior.
A data-inventory check maps every persistent category to exactly one source of truth and one accountable owner.
Access tests and configuration evidence show approved access succeeds and access outside each recorded boundary is denied.
Time-bounded tests or observed evidence demonstrate the approved retention, deletion, and audit outcomes for every stored category.
A timed fixture recreation rehearsal meets the approved RTO and RPO.
A traceability check maps every applicable constraint to a validation, migration, or rollback check.
A rendered-output test confirms the approved outcome is displayed.
GIVEN input outside approved constraints, WHEN the application receives it, THEN the input is rejected and approved state is unchanged.
IaC validation and environment-specific configuration checks pass for every approved environment.
The runbook check confirms the artifact, order, health checks, failure boundary, and authorized next action are explicit.
Evidence checks confirm required signals, thresholds, destinations, and zero secret values in sampled content.
The runbook check identifies one responsible owner and one actionable escalation path for each material incident class.
Rehearsal or observed evidence covers rollback, retained resources, and the approved teardown result.
Each target names the path, percentile or bound, workload, and observable test result.
A bounded test or calculation covers the approved normal and peak workload for every environment.
Tests or configuration checks show work stays within approved limits and fails safely at each boundary.
The profile records data shape, duration, concurrency, environment, and pass condition, or records why performance evidence does not apply.
Generated failure-sequence tests never exceed the configured timeout and retry bounds.
GIVEN work that may be delivered more than once, WHEN the same work is delivered repeatedly, THEN one effective outcome is recorded.
Stateful concurrency property tests preserve the newer valid state across the approved generated-case bound.
A timed fixture recreation rehearsal meets the approved RTO and RPO.
A rollback rehearsal restores the bound last known-good artifact and all approved smoke tests pass.
GIVEN an approved protected operation, WHEN a signed-in or signed-out identity requests it, THEN the signed-in request succeeds and the signed-out request is denied.
Authorization tests prove approved access succeeds and unapproved access is denied at the recorded identity boundary.
Secret scans pass and reviewed generated artifacts and logs contain zero secret values.
GIVEN invalid, malformed, or oversized external input, WHEN the application receives it, THEN the request is rejected and no unintended state change is recorded.
Policy checks and deployed access tests confirm required actions succeed and actions outside the approved resource boundary are denied.
Infrastructure definitions and deployed configuration checks match every approved encryption control.
Audit-event tests and log review confirm all five required event conditions for every sampled event.
Configuration or teardown evidence confirms the approved idle behavior for every applicable resource.
A design review identifies material movement and retention and records a requirement basis for each retained path.
Expansion evidence cites the approved utilization trigger and an observed measurement at or above that trigger.
A traceability check links the affected requirement and design IDs, evidence, and owner decision.
